FINDING_ID: DimRet_F001
SEVERITY: 0.82
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.75
DESCRIPTION: The `aggregate_per_model_mu` method uses maximum aggregation ("as long as ANY single model is still delivering value"), but this contradicts the design principle that "premature stopping is worse than one extra round." With max aggregation, a single poorly-performing model (low mu) that is benched but still has non-zero mu (e.g., 0.01) will keep the system running indefinitely, even when all active models have zero marginal value. The conservative bias should be MINIMUM across active models (any model showing exhaustion triggers stop), not maximum. The documentation states conservative bias but implements the opposite.
PROPOSED_FIX: Change `aggregate_per_model_mu` to return minimum of active models' mu values, not maximum. Alternatively, use weighted average by model costs.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: DimRet_F002
SEVERITY: 0.76
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.68
DESCRIPTION: The `remaining_value_estimate` method uses `smoothed_marginal_value(round_idx - 1)` for decay computation but applies smoothing window W. When round_idx < W, the smoothing window shrinks (start = max(0, round_idx - W + 1)). This causes `mu_prev` to be computed over a different window size than `mu_current`, breaking the decay ratio's consistency. For early rounds (r < W), decay ratios become unstable and can produce extreme values that affect the forecast.
PROPOSED_FIX: Ensure consistent window size: compute mu_current and mu_prev both with full W rounds of data, or use unsmoothed mu for decay calculation in early rounds.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: DimRet_F003
SEVERITY: 0.70
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72
DESCRIPTION: The per-area vocabulary tracking uses `str(f.flaw_class)` as area proxy, but flaw classes (1-8) don't map to the six management areas. This creates misalignment: findings from different management areas may be grouped under same flaw class, while single area may produce findings across multiple flaw classes. The "area" concept in Phase D (Exp14) refers to management areas (Role Assignment, Load Balancing, etc.), not flaw categories.
PROPOSED_FIX: Add `area_id` field to `Finding` class or pass area context explicitly when calling `add_round_from_findings`. Use actual area identifiers (1-6 or names).
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: DimRet_F004
SEVERITY: 0.65
FLAW_CLASS: 6
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.60
DESCRIPTION: The `novelty_rate` computation compares each new finding against ALL prior findings (O(n²)). With cumulative findings growing linearly, novelty detection becomes quadratic in round count. For experiments with hundreds of findings, this becomes computationally prohibitive. The `tau_novelty` threshold (0.8) is also undocumented in config—default value unknown.
PROPOSED_FIX: Use locality-sensitive hashing or sampling for large n. Document `tau_novelty` in `DynamicManagementConfig` with sensible default (e.g., 0.7).
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: DimRet_F005
SEVERITY: 0.58
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.55
DESCRIPTION: The `add_round` and `add_round_from_findings` methods both write to `_cumulative_yields` dict, but `add_round_from_findings` also updates novelty/vocab tracking. If caller mixes both methods for same round_idx, internal state becomes inconsistent: novelty/vocab updates may occur without corresponding yield entry (if `add_round` called after `add_round_from_findings` overwrites yield). No protection against duplicate round_idx registration.
PROPOSED_FIX: Make `add_round` private, expose only `add_round_from_findings`. Or add check: `if round_idx in self._cumulative_yields: raise ValueError("Round already registered")`.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: DimRet_F006
SEVERITY: 0.73
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.70
DESCRIPTION: The `_abstraction_dropping` method is defined but never called in `stop()` predicate, violating the "CONJUNCTIVE ascending abstraction guard" documented in design decisions. Abstraction drop should be a conjunctive factor with other signals (mu, novelty, vocab), but currently has no effect on stop decision.
PROPOSED_FIX: Modify `stop()` to include `self._abstraction_dropping(round_idx)` as an additional disjunctive term (or conjunctive factor as intended). Clarify requirement: "stop requires (mu<tau OR novelty<tau OR vocab_saturated) AND abstraction_dropping"?
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: DimRet_F007
SEVERITY: 0.68
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.65
DESCRIPTION: The `vocab_saturated` method's fallback to global vocab tracking when `self._area_vocab` is empty creates a silent behavior change. During blind round (no area differentiation), it uses global vocab. When areas become differentiated (later rounds), it switches to per-area logic. This can cause discontinuity: blind round may show saturation (global) while per-area tracking would not. No warning or logging of this transition.
PROPOSED_FIX: Maintain consistent policy: either always use per-area tracking (initialize with default area) or document the transition and add logging when switching.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: DimRet_F008
[CROSS-COMPONENT, UNVERIFIED FROM THIS SCOPE]
SEVERITY: 0.80
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.78
DESCRIPTION: The `ConvergenceDetector` and `DiminishingReturnsDetector` both track novelty but with different similarity thresholds (`tau_sim` vs `tau_novelty`). This creates inconsistency: a finding may be "novel" for convergence (similarity < tau_sim) but "not novel" for diminishing returns (similarity >= tau_novelty), causing detectors to disagree on whether content is exhausted. The thresholds are independent config parameters with no coordination.
PROPOSED_FIX: Align similarity thresholds or derive `tau_novelty` from `tau_sim` (e.g., `tau_novelty = tau_sim - 0.1`). Document relationship.
VERIFIED: FALSE
